title: Mutton Karahi

seo.title: Authentic Mutton Karahi Recipe | Easy Pakistani Dinner
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of authentic Pakistani Mutton Karahi with our easy-to-follow recipe. Perfect for a flavorful dinner, this dish is rich, spicy, and incredibly delicious.
h2Headings: Tips for the Perfect Mutton Karahi
seo.imageAlt: A delicious plate of authentic Pakistani Mutton Karahi, garnished with ginger and green chilies, ready to be served.
seo.imageCaption: Savor the rich and spicy flavors of homemade Mutton Karahi, a classic Pakistani dinner dish.

description: Mutton Karahi is a beloved Pakistani delicacy, known for its rich, spicy, and tangy tomato-based gravy. This traditional dish is slow-cooked to perfection, allowing the tender mutton to absorb all the aromatic spices. It's an unforgettable culinary experience, best enjoyed with fresh naan or roti for a truly authentic taste of Pakistan.

instructions.title: Prepare Mutton and Brown
instructions.text: Heat oil in a large karahi or heavy-bottomed pot over high heat. Add the mutton pieces and fry until they turn light brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. This seals in the juices and adds flavor.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add the ginger garlic paste to the mutton and fry for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the paste.

instructions.title: Incorporate Tomatoes and Spices
instructions.text: Add the chopped or pureed tomatoes, salt, red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Mix well. Cover the pot and cook on medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes, or until the tomatoes soften and release their water, and the oil separates from the masala.

instructions.title: Tenderize the Mutton
instructions.text: Stir in the green chilies and black pepper powder. If using, add the whisked yogurt now and mix thoroughly. Add about 1/2 cup of water, cover, and cook on low heat until the mutton is tender. This can take 20-30 minutes depending on the mutton quality. Add more water if needed to prevent burning and ensure tenderness.

instructions.title: Finish the Karahi
instructions.text: Once the mutton is tender and the gravy has reached your desired consistency, uncover and increase the heat to medium-high. Fry the karahi for a few minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil completely separates from the gravy and the masala is well roasted. Stir in the garam masala powder.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove from heat. Garnish generously with julienned fresh ginger and chopped fresh coriander. Serve hot with fresh naan, roti, or chapati for an authentic Pakistani dinner experience.

tips: For truly tender mutton, consider using a pressure cooker for step 4. It can reduce cooking time significantly, but always ensure the meat is fully tender before proceeding.
Adjust the amount of green chilies and red chili powder to your preferred spice level. For a milder karahi, deseed the green chilies.
Always fry the masala well until the oil separates; this is key to developing the deep, rich flavor and texture characteristic of a good Karahi.
